answer.evidence: The main body spans rows 13-22 at a constant width of 28. Its column scan is a vertical shading gradient: row 14 mid-teal, rows 15-17 light, row 18 brightest highlight, rows 19-22 progressively darker. That reads as one side face of a cushion seen face-on, not a horizontal seat seen from above. Row 13 is only the outline plus a 1-row rim, with no band ending in a front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. The headrest block (rows 11-13) is likewise a flat face. The lamp and rinse bowl are thin vertical details. The pedestal below (rows 23-29) is a narrow stem and base. The seat surface cannot be seen from above, so this is a side elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a compact two-tile prop. Its measured facts sit at or above the simpler Beodeul references: 12 colours per tile against 10 for the hedge, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. That means the outline is tinted (dark blue-teal beside the cushion, dark grey-blue beside the metal), not a black sticker line. The teal cushion shows a highlight, a mid tone and a dark underside with a darker shadow, about 4 steps. The grey lamp and base have light, mid and dark steps. No large area is one flat colour. The 17 total colours are well below the stall (40) and well (38). The shading is a little smoother and less speckled than the richest references, so density is slightly lower. For its size and simplicity it would sit acceptably next to the hedge and bench without looking flatter or more sticker-like.

answer.evidence: The long teal cushion has a lighter top band at rows 14-18 (light fill at rows 14-17). A bright 1-row front-edge line at row 18 ends that band. Darker teal at rows 19-21 reads as eave shadow and front face, and the face continues to the outline at row 22. A pedestal and base at rows 23-29 support it, so the front/support height is 3+ rows. The body is a long horizontal cushion with a visible top plane, so it is not a flat slab or a bare front elevation. The lamp, arm and rinse bowl are small details and do not change the main body reading. The head-end block at rows 11-13 is minor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, clean-edged chair with a teal body, pale grey-blue lamp arm and a white or grey bowl. It has 17 distinct colours in total, against 38-40 for the stall and well. Its per-tile median of 12 is above the hedge (10) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline has a colour tint rather than being black. Structurally, though, each material has only about 3 steps (highlight, mid, dark), where Beodeul uses 5-6 per material. The teal seat and backrest are mostly smooth bands with a single highlight line. They have no grain, speckle or per-element shading like the stall's awning stripes and goods or the well's stones. The overhead lamp and rinse bowl are simple shapes with minimal shading. The measured numbers are acceptable, but the shading is shallower and the texture sparser than the best references. Because of that thin ramp depth, I fail it when in doubt.
